data.name: Garden Fresh Vegetable Omelette
data.description: Tender, golden eggs envelop vibrant diced bell peppers, earthy sautéed mushrooms, and silky wilted baby spinach, delivering a savory, aromatic breakfast with a fluffy curd texture.

items.name: egg
items.notes: purchase weight 170g in shell; edible yield 150g liquid egg

items.name: red bell pepper
items.notes: requires approximately 55g whole pepper to yield 40g edible dice after removing stem and seeds

items.name: cremini mushroom
items.notes: requires approximately 40g whole mushrooms to yield 35g edible slices after trimming dry stem bases

items.name: scallion
items.notes: requires approximately 20g whole scallion to yield 15g edible slices after trimming root tips

instructions.text: Place the red bell pepper, cremini mushrooms, and scallions on a cutting board, then finely dice the pepper into 5 mm cubes, slice the mushrooms into 3 mm slices, and slice the scallions finely.
tips: Keeping vegetable pieces small ensures they soften rapidly and do not puncture the delicate egg envelope when folding.

instructions.text: Crack the 3 eggs into a medium mixing bowl, add 15 ml of cold water, 1 g of fine sea salt, and 0.5 g of freshly ground black pepper, then whisk vigorously for 60 seconds until completely uniform with no visible streaks of albumen.

doneness_cues.visual: Uniform pale yellow liquid with a light layer of micro-bubbles across the surface.

tips: Water creates internal steam during cooking to produce a fluffier curd without adding dairy proteins that can scorch.

instructions.text: Place a 20 cm nonstick skillet over medium heat at 160°C (320°F) and add 5 ml of olive oil, tilting the pan to coat the bottom surface.
Add the diced red bell pepper and sliced cremini mushrooms to the skillet and sauté for 3 minutes until softened and their released moisture has evaporated.

doneness_cues.visual: Mushrooms are browned at edges and no liquid puddles remain in the pan.
doneness_cues.tactile: Peppers are tender-crisp when pressed with the spatula.

instructions.text: Add the baby spinach, sliced scallions, and remaining 0.5 g of fine sea salt to the skillet, stirring for 1 minute until the spinach leaves have fully collapsed.

doneness_cues.visual: Spinach is wilted and dark green with zero pooled water.

instructions.text: Transfer the sautéed vegetables from the skillet onto a clean plate and set aside at room temperature.
Wipe the skillet surface clean with a paper towel, return it to medium-low heat at 150°C (300°F), and add the remaining 5 ml of olive oil, spreading it thoroughly across the pan.
Pour the whisked egg mixture into the center of the warm skillet, allowing it to spread out naturally to the edges.

Using the heat-resistant silicone spatula, gently push the cooked outer edges of the eggs toward the center while tilting the skillet to allow raw liquid egg to flow underneath onto the hot surface, repeating for 90 seconds until soft, moist curds form across the pan.

doneness_cues.visual: Soft, glistening curds across the base with very little loose liquid on top.

instructions.text: Smooth the curds into an even disc, cover the skillet with a lid, lower the heat to low at 130°C (265°F), and cook for 90 seconds until the eggs are firm throughout and an instant-read food thermometer inserted into the center registers at least 71°C (160°F).

doneness_cues.visual: Egg surface is set with no runny liquid remaining.
doneness_cues.tactile: Top springs back gently when lightly touched.

tips: Covering traps gentle residual steam to bring the top to the safe 71°C (160°F) threshold without scorching the bottom.

instructions.text: Remove the lid and spoon the cooked vegetable mixture across one half of the set egg disc, leaving a 1 cm border along the outer rim.
Slide the silicone spatula under the unfilled half of the omelette and gently fold it over the vegetable filling to create a half-moon shape.
Tilt the skillet toward the serving plate and ease the folded omelette onto the plate, serving immediately.
